description: Musical instruments hold a significant place in Indian Classical Music. Knowledge of major musical instruments and their famous exponents is crucial for SSC and other competitive exams.

sections.title: Traditional Classification of Musical Instruments
sections.description: According to Bharat Muni's Natya Shastra, Indian musical instruments are primarily classified into four categories.

key_concepts.explanation: Instruments where sound is produced by the vibration of strings. Examples: Sitar, Sarod, Veena, Santoor, Sarangi.
Instruments where sound is produced by blowing air. Examples: Flute, Shehnai, Nadaswaram.
Instruments covered with animal skin or membrane that produce sound when struck. Examples: Tabla, Pakhawaj, Dholak, Mridangam.
Solid instruments made of metal, wood, or clay that are struck against each other. Examples: Manjira, Ghatam, Jaltarang.

sections.title: Important Facts of the Music World
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts related to musicians, instruments, and their highest honors.

important_facts.fact: Ustad Bismillah Khan (Shehnai) was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001.
Pt. Ravi Shankar (Sitar) was the first Indian to win a Grammy Award (in 1968 for the album 'West Meets East').
M. S. Subbulakshmi (Carnatic Vocalist) was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna in 1998.
Pt. Bhimsen Joshi (Vocalist) was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008; he belonged to the Kirana Gharana.
The Sarod was invented by the ancestors of Ustad Amjad Ali Khan by modifying an ancient instrument called the Rabab.
